chapter_title: [Concerning the Five] War[s that the] Sons of [Li]

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
The first conflict is the first direct engagement of living good against the central dominion of evil and all the subordinate evils that had issued from a full sufficiency of fundamental falsities. Living good pursued and enclosed them by the living inward faculty that discerns and binds, so that their evils and falsities were held fast within a fixed restraint. Pure and uncorrupted love stood openly against them, and the living ardor of that love made their escape impossible; for the whole sufficiency of their contrivances, rising from the full set of elemental falsities, was seized and shut in. Then living good struck at their origin, removing the beginning-source of their organized perversions, and cut off the root-principle of evil with decisive force.

The second conflict is that of Divine operation in living power, which formed an ordered heaven and established the arrangement of goods and truths in their proper degrees. It disposed the rebellious dominations into their assigned states and bound them in an intermediate region, fixing their influences within a complete ordering of cognitions and ultimates, held inside the full structure of the three degrees of life. For those dominations rose up in resistance, wishing to evade restraint because they understood that Divine power can bind by an unbreakable connection. Yet Divine operation confronted them by many modes of presence, by a fullness of ordered powers, by abundant means of action, and by severe counteraction against their violence; and by wisdom in application it shut them in. Not one of them was able to rescue itself, and all their attempted evasions were brought to nothing; therefore, because their resistance was foreseen and met, they were taken in their own devices and held fast.

The third conflict is that of mediating Divine truth making itself visible and effective in the lower degree. It gathered up into itself all remaining good and truth, together with whatever spiritual quality had been carried off into what consumes, reclaiming it from the entire pretended dominion; and it laid bare that dominion’s exaltation, by which it had gloried in the pride of seeming illumination and spread its influence outward. Then a power came against it that was able to overcome, and it stripped that dominion of everything it boasted as its own—its accumulated cognitions, its glittering falsifications, and its arrogance and wanton delight in ruling.

Such is the nature of that pretended dominion: it steals every abundance, claiming as its own whatever goods and truths pass through the mind, and it lives by borrowing appearances as it moves along the ways of thought. Therefore what had been taken was cleansed and purified, with the living separated from the defiled and made clean.

The fourth conflict is that of Divine truth fully present in the human, waging against all rebellious impulses in the inner and outer degrees. When the reclaimed good and truth had been purified from those impulses through mediating revelation, the restraints that held the disorder in check began to loosen and the rebellion rose up again. Then the glorified Divine met the uprising of the whole pretended dominion. It invested itself anew with the full order of truth for combat and bound the disorder again; it rebuilt the whole framework of spiritual life and fixed a great contest in which the rebellious power was humbled and held firm. In this it fulfilled the will of the supreme Divine, and it gave hope to the first human state, offering preservation and conveyance for whatever remnant of living good and truth could still be saved.

The fifth conflict is that of the living counsel that flows from the Divine, which is the inward call toward good together with the reception that obeys. This counsel entered with great force into the ultimate and lowest degree and set a firm confirmation against the bonds of spiritual death that cling there. It prevailed over the persuasive compulsion toward spiritual death forever, and it established the reign of life and light.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the chapter by establishing the initial victory of living good over the full array of fundamental falsities and their organized dominion.
paragraph_translations.notes: Some phrases in the source are fragmentary; the sense of a decisive enclosure, witness of pure love, and cutting off the origin is clear enough to translate as a unified spiritual action.

paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by moving from the first binding of evil to the orderly fixing of rebellious influences within the full structure of degrees.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source mixes cosmological placement language with combat; translated as ordering and restriction within degrees, with multiple modes of Divine presence. One clause appears corrupt (“he {...} [did not prevail]”), but the thrust is that the rebels did not succeed.

paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from restraint and placement to reclamation of mixed goods and truths and the exposure and plundering of pretended dominion.
paragraph_translations.notes: The identity of “a person…powerful against it” is functionally an overcoming influx; kept impersonal to preserve spiritual sense. Several bracketed bits are unclear but converge on exposure of pride and stripping of claimed riches.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by summarizing the character of evil dominion and the consequent purification of what it had appropriated.
paragraph_translations.notes: The brief comparative line (“like a thief”) translates cleanly as the proprial appropriation of passing goods and truths; “paths” rendered as progressions of thought.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by portraying a renewed uprising after purification and the subsequent re-binding and restoration of spiritual order, culminating in hope for the remnant.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source contains several broken phrases; translated by preserving the sequence: purification → loosening → uprising → re-arming with truth → rebuilding order → hope to the first human state and preservation of the remnant.

paragraph_translations.translation: The fifth conflict is that of the living counsel that flows from the Divine, which is the inward call toward good together with the reception that obeys. paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES to the final and conclusive victory by which Divine counsel secures the ultimates against death-persuasion and establishes lasting governance of life.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Persuasion” and “summons and obedience” cohere as compelling influx versus obedient reception; “seal upon the earth and the depth” translates as firm confirmation in ultimates.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coheres strongly as a fivefold progression: initial binding of evil, orderly fixation of rebellious influences across degrees, reclamation and exposure of stolen goods and truths, renewed rebellion met by glorified Divine truth restoring the framework, and finally a decisive securing of ultimates against death-persuasion. The voice is consistent though several source clauses are fragmentary; those breaks do not alter the overall spiritual sequence.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential substrate: warfare is taught by function (binding, sealing, netting, cutting roots). The spiritual reading does not stumble here; the narrative is organic and self-interpreting.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by what powers DO: “He hunted them with his net, which is the living soul. He [bound them] in the snare and [sealed them]… the living fire [shone forth]… He cut and dug out the root of the five trees.” The reading’s notes: “fragmentary; the sense… is clear enough… unified spiritual action.” This is exactly the correspondential mode: net/soul binds; fire prevents escape; roots/trees indicate origins cut off.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly correspondential, but with localized cosmological-placement diction that edges toward administrative ordering (stations/placements) and a small damaged clause. The reading ‘smooths’ it into a degrees-schema; the stumble is primarily due to damage plus a brief voice-mix, not a later insertion that can be cleanly removed.
findings.evidence: Correspondential combat continues (“rebelled… wished to flee… bind and fetter… appeared… with many aspects… imprisoned them with much skill”), but the middle becomes schematic placement: “spread out the rulers and chained them in the middle [of the firmament]… set them in the three vessels.” That is closer to governance/arrangement than functional correspondence, and the reading admits the seam: “mixes cosmological placement language with combat,” plus corruption: “One clause appears corrupt (‘he {...} [did not prevail]’).” If you delete the placement lines, the fight narrative would still read, but the chapter’s own ‘five wars’ list is already cosmological-mythic, so this looks like an original mixed register rather than a Mani-style administrative overlay block.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential substrate with an embedded simile and functional ‘theft/purification’ logic. No narrative break; the “person…powerful against it” is a typical substrate indirection (function > personal identity) and does not require administrative names.
findings.evidence: Text: “Third Ambassador… gathered up… all light… uncovered… pride… A person comes, who is powerful… he stripped him, silver [gold]…” followed by functional moral definition: “the ruling-power… like a thief… as they travel through the paths… He cleansed and purified it.” The reading explicitly handles this without forcing identities: “kept impersonal to preserve spiritual sense,” and ¶5 “translates cleanly as the proprial appropriation… and consequent purification.” That is classic correspondential teaching by action and effect (stealing → cleansing), not by jurisdiction lists.

findings.diagnosis: Insertion into a functional narrative: christological/historical identification (“Jesus the glorious one”) and Adam/remnant/‘light ship’ language looks like a systematizing, salvation-historical overlay at the seam of an otherwise functional combat-restoration sequence. The spiritual reading can still make sense of it, but it must generalize heavily (“Divine truth fully present in the human… first human state… remnant”)—a sign the text has shifted to a different didactic mode.
findings.evidence: The paragraph begins with a named, title-bearing figure: “the fourth war is this that Jesus the glorious one waged…”—a move from functional agents (net/soul, fire, binding) to a christological label. It then introduces salvation-history tokens: “he gave the] hope to Adam [the remnant] to his light ship.” Those elements do not participate in the chapter’s own functional mechanism of binding/purifying; they reposition the war as reassurance to a named primordial recipient. The reading’s notes acknowledge reconstruction pressure: “source contains several broken phrases; translated by preserving the sequence… culminating in hope… preservation of the remnant,” i.e., it has to supply a theological through-line across broken phrases, which is typical when an overlay has been stitched into a damaged substrate seam.
findings.scope: "The fourth war is this that Jesus the glorious one waged against all the rebels who had rebelled above and below." … and the closing salvation-historical clause: "[he gave the] hope to Adam [the remnant] to his light ship."

findings.diagnosis: Administrative overlay block: defines the fifth war in institutional/governance terms (“counsel of life,” “summons and obedience,” “placed its seal,” “bonds of death,” “gave the kingdom”). This is not taught by correspondence from functions of natural things but by named administrative mechanisms and legal actions (seal, counsel, kingdom). The spiritual reading explicitly has to reinterpret institutional phrases as interior faculties, which is a typical ‘stumble’ indicator of voice mismatch.
findings.evidence: Text is dominated by governance/institution vocabulary rather than functional imagery: “the counsel of life… the summons and the obedience… placed [its seal] upon the [earth] and the [depth]… the bonds of death… it gave the kingdom [of life and of light].” Unlike ¶2’s net/fire/root, there is no natural-functional basis given for why ‘summons-and-obedience’ correspond to an inner process; the reading admits it is doing conceptual mapping: “‘Persuasion’ and ‘summons and obedience’ cohere as compelling influx versus obedient reception,” which is a harmonization move over administrative phrasing. As a block, it does not interrupt a nearby correspondential chain (it is the whole fifth item), so it fits the “overlay block” pattern: keep text, flag voice.
findings.scope: Annotate all of ¶7 as an administrative/institutional layer (counsel/summons/obedience/seal/kingdom framing) rather than correspondential substrate.

textual_criticism.summary: 5 findings: ¶2 and ¶4-¶5 are clean correspondential substrate (no action). ¶3 is mixed/damaged but not best treated as insertion (no action). Two disruptions: ¶6 contains a likely christological/salvation-historical expansion at a seam (recommend excision of the ‘Jesus the glorious one’ identification and the Adam/remnant/light-ship clause). ¶7 is a full administrative overlay block (recommend annotate, not excise).

harmonized_paragraphs.text: The first war is that of the First living Man, which he waged against the King of the realms of Darkness, and all the rulers that had come forth from the five worlds of Darkness. He hunted them with his net, which is the living soul. He bound them in the snare and sealed them the face of the Virgin of Light his virgin, the living fire shone forth, so that they did not find how to escape his net because he caught them like fish in the sea of smoke the five counsels of the five elements and seized. He cut and dug out the root of the five trees, root of the evil tree, like an axe.

The second war is that of the Living Spirit which he waged against the rulers and the firmaments. He has constructed the things and the worlds of light; he spread out the rulers and chained them in the middle of the firmament the stars in all the earths and he set them in the three vessels. For the rulers rebelled and were set against the Living Spirit. They wished to flee since they knew and realised that he might bind and fetter them with a strong chain. Yet he, the Living Spirit, appeared to them with many aspects, with numerous powers, with many hands and great cruelties. He was revealed to them, he imprisoned them with much skill. Not one of them was able to save himself, and he did not prevail. Now, since he all of them he trapped them had foreseen their rebellion by their own devices.

The third war is that of the Third Ambassador who has displayed his image in the height what is below and he gathered up scooped and he all light and the property of the rulers the ones that are consumed from the entire ruling-power and he uncovered pride of the light and the extending it over the whole. A person comes, who is powerful against it; he takes his riches and he stripped him, silver gold, his pride and wantonness.
This is what the ruling-power is like: it is like a thief, all riches that it takes as they travel through the paths light by borrowed. He cleansed and purified it.

The fourth war is this that he waged against all the rebels who had rebelled above and below. When the light was purified from them by the image of the Third Ambassador, their chains loosened and they rose up. The glorious one in the fourth war; he came and brought and he restrained a rebellion of the entire ruling-power. He girded himself with the armour of truth all of it another time. He constructed the whole structure and he made and he bound a great contest; he humiliated therein. it firm he fulfilled the will of the greatness.

The fifth war is this that the counsel of life waged against the persuasion which is the summons and the obedience and the great counsel great its power and it placed its seal upon the earth and the depth the bonds of death, which clung with it. And it was victorious over the persuasion for ever, and it gave the kingdom of life and of light.

changes_summary: Implemented Finding 4 (¶6, excise): removed the christological/historical identification “Jesus the glorious one” from the opening clause, and removed the closing salvation-historical clause about giving hope to Adam, the remnant, and the light ship. Minimal grammatical smoothing was applied to keep ¶6 coherent after excision. No other changes: Findings 1–3 and 5 recommended none/annotate only, so ¶2–¶5 and ¶7 remain unchanged.
